question: Which of the following statements is correct? 1. The eleventh Spirit (精魄) obtained by the player in Chapter 2 is Mad Tiger (疯虎). 2. The first Spirit (精魄) obtained by the player in Chapter 2 is Earth Wolf (地狼). 3. The second Spirit (精魄) obtained by the player in Chapter 4 is Lantern Ghost. 4. The last Spirit (精魄) obtained by the player in Chapter 3 is Non-Pure (不净).

rollouts.answer: Statement 4 (Non-Pure/不净 is the last spirit of chapter 3).

clip_qa answered 'No' -- claimed the boss dissolves and the character continues without a visible spirit pickup, directly contradicting what rollouts 1 and 3's clip_qa calls on the same/overlapping window found (a 疯虎 pickup at ~20617s)

rollouts.failure_point: Visual sub-agent (clip_qa) misread the 20370-20460s clip and reported no spirit acquisition after the Mad Tiger fight, so the agent ruled out the correct statement 1 and fell back on weak, unconfirmed SQL matches near 39240s to justify statement 4 instead.
rollouts.evidence_checked: sql on event_steps around 20500-20700s confirms a boss-defeat loot panel (20580-20610s) followed by a spirit-selection screen (20610-20670s, 'selects 幽魂 and 窃魂 spirits'); the literal string 疯虎/地狼/不净 do not appear in event_steps.description at all, only in episodes text as a boss label -- so this statement can only be resolved by watching the actual pickup screen, which is exactly what this rollout's clip_qa got wrong.

rollouts.answer: Statement 3 (灯笼鬼/血灯鬼 is the second spirit obtained in chapter 4).

rollouts.failure_point: Found direct visual confirmation of statement 1 (Mad Tiger spirit pickup at ~20617s) but did not attempt the ordinal count needed to check '11th'; instead picked statement 3 based on an unverified ordinal claim ('second') for 血灯鬼, when its own scan of the preceding chapter-4 window found zero other spirit pickups -- so 血灯鬼 was at best the first spirit found in that window, not confirmed second.
rollouts.evidence_checked: Same as rollout 0/db_evidence: 血灯鬼 literally appears in event_steps.description at 46830-46860s (matches clue interval 46834-46850), which is why this is a tempting distractor, but nothing in the DB or the rollout's own clip_qa calls establishes an ordinal 'second' position for it.

rollouts.answer: Statement 3 (血灯鬼 is the second spirit obtained in chapter 4).

rollouts.evidence_checked: sql confirms zero event_steps rows contain the literal string 地狼 anywhere in the whole DB, so this rollout's claim that Earth Wolf is the first chapter-2 spirit has no retrievable textual support at all -- it was never actually checked, visually or otherwise.

db_evidence.notes: The four spirit names in the question (疯虎, 地狼, 不净, 灯笼鬼/血灯鬼) are largely absent as literal strings from the structured tables: event_steps.description contains 0 rows for 疯虎, 地狼, or 不净, and only 2 rows for 血灯鬼 (at 46830-46860s, matching clue interval 3). episodes text mentions 疯虎 only as a boss label at 20340-20520s, not as a spirit-pickup name. This means the ground truth for statements 1, 2 and 4 is retrievable only by watching the actual pickup-notification frames via clip_qa around the clue intervals and, for the ordinal ('11th', 'first', 'last') claims, by exhaustively counting every spirit pickup in the surrounding chapter with repeated clip_qa calls across the whole chapter span -- something only rollout 3 did. Statement 3's clue interval (血灯鬼 loot at 46830-46860s) is the one fact that IS directly retrievable via plain SQL/semantic search, which made it an attractive but ordinal-unverified distractor for rollouts 1 and 2.

root_causes: The question requires an ordinal count ('the 11th spirit', 'the first spirit', 'the last spirit') over spirits scattered across an entire chapter (tens of minutes), but the structured DB text (event_steps/episodes) almost never names the spirits literally, so the only reliable path is exhaustive clip_qa scanning of the whole chapter in <=20-minute windows -- expensive and only rollout 3 actually did it.

The single most retrievable fact in the DB (血灯鬼 loot text at 46830-46860s, matching clue interval 3) is a distractor: it is real and easy to find via SQL, but statement 3 additionally requires confirming it is specifically the SECOND spirit of chapter 4, which none of the failing rollouts verified before submitting.

The visual sub-agent (clip_qa) is not deterministic across rollouts on the same evidence window: asked essentially the same question about a spirit pickup after the Mad Tiger boss fight (~20370-20680s), rollout 0 answered 'No spirit visible' while rollouts 1 and 3 answered 'Yes, 疯虎 pickup at ~20617s' -- this single visual misread in rollout 0 flipped it from a correct to an incorrect final answer.

Two rollouts (2 and 4) never invoked clip_qa or the visual-verification skill at all despite the counting-and-ordering / locating-time-intervals skills both being read, and submitted an answer based only on SQL/semantic-search text hits, which for this DB cannot establish the ordinal claims needed.
what_worked: Rollout 3 followed the 'counting-and-ordering' and 'visual-verification' skills literally: it built an ordered, exhaustive inventory of every spirit pickup across chapter 2 via ~15 sequential clip_qa calls in <=1500s windows, which is the only way to actually verify an '11th spirit' ordinal claim.

Rollout 3 also used clip_qa to positively rule out statement 2 (confirming the true first chapter-2 spirit is not 地狼) rather than relying on the absence of a DB text match, which is a weaker/negative-evidence argument.
transferable_lessons: For ordinal claims ('the Nth X obtained', 'the first/last X'), do not stop at finding one matching event near the stated clue interval -- explicitly count all preceding occurrences via clip_qa across the whole relevant chapter/timespan before accepting the ordinal.

Treat a literal SQL/text keyword match near a clue interval as a candidate, not a conclusion, when the question asks about ordinal position (e.g. 'second spirit') -- verify the position, not just the identity, with clip_qa.

When a spirit/item name never appears in event_steps.description or episodes text anywhere in the DB, that is itself a signal the claim can only be resolved visually; route to clip_qa immediately rather than continuing broad semantic_search/run_sql sweeps.

clip_qa answers on the same time window are not fully reliable across independent calls (one rollout reported 'no spirit visible' where two others found one); when a visual answer is decisive and surprising (e.g. it rules out an option that literal boss-encounter text suggests should have a reward), consider a repeat/cross-check clip_qa call before committing.
open_questions: Whether rollout 0's clip_qa 'No spirit visible' answer at 20370-20460s was a genuine visual miss (e.g. the pickup notification appears slightly outside that exact sub-window) or a hallucination, since rollout 1/3's clip_qa on an overlapping/wider window (20370-20680s) did find it -- could not independently re-run clip_qa here to confirm which framing was at fault.
